entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Convened via Kenya Gazette Notice No.4465 of 26th June, 2020)

entries.label: other
entries.text: The House met at the Senate Chamber, Parliament Buildings, at 2.30 p.m.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members! Sen. (Dr.) Ali, let us have some order!

entries.label: heading
entries.text: CONVENING OF SPECIAL SITTING TO CONSIDER BILLS AND THIRD BASIS FOR REVENUE SHARING AMONG COUNTIES

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Hon. Senators, on the request of the Senate Majority Leader via a letter referenced No.SEN/ML/2020/26/6 dated 26th June, 2020, and with the support of the requisite number of Senators, I appointed today, Tuesday, 30th June, 2020, as a day for a Special Sitting of the Senate vide Gazette Notice N0.4465 dated 26th June, 2020. In the Gazette Notice, I indicated that the business to be transacted at this Special Sitting shall be- (1) The National Drought Management Authority (Amendment) Bill (National Assembly Bills No.26 of 2019);

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Members, you may take your seats.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Senators entered the Chamber and took their seats)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (2) The Pandemic Response and Management Bill (Senate Bills No.6 of 2020)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. (Eng.) Maina walked into the Chamber and sat on an undesignated seat)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: An Hon. Senator
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: That is not a designated seat, Sen. (Eng.) Maina. Sit on a designated seat.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. (Eng.) Maina sat on a designated seat)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: (3) The Kenya Medical Supplies Authority (Amendment) Bill (Senate Bills No. 38 of 2018); (4) The Cancer Prevention and Control (Amendment) Bill (Senate Bills No.9 of 2019); (5) The National Assembly Amendments to the Petition to County Assemblies (Procedure) Bill (Senate Bills No.22 of 2018); (6) The National Assembly Amendments to the County Early Childhood Education Bill (Senate Bills No.26 of 2018); and, (7) The Third Basis for Revenue Allocation among the County Governments.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Hon. Senators, from the onset, I wish to draw you to Standing Order No.116 on Disorderly Conduct. It says- "(1) A Senator is disorderly if the Senator-- (a) creates disorder; (b) knowingly raises a false point of order; (c) unnecessarily interrupts proceedings or consults in a disruptive manner; (d) fails to record abstention in a Division; (e) makes allegations without, in the Speaker's opinion, adequate substantiation; or (f) commits any other breach of these Stranding Orders that in the opinion of the Speaker, constitutes disorderly conduct." I appeal to you that we should not get to where I am forced to apply this Standing Order so that we are able to proceed in an orderly manner. Let us move on to the next Order.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Let us have the Chairperson of the Committee on Finance and Budget.

entries.label: heading
entries.text: REPORT ON THE THIRD BASIS FOR REVENUE ALLOCATION AMONG COUNTY GOVERNMENTS

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Sen. (Dr.) Ali
entries.text: Where is he? He should be here!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: He is not here? Let us move on to the next Order.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order Members! Before you proceed, I will allow the Chairperson of the Committee on Finance and Budget to table the report which has been brought. Any Member of the Committee? Who is the Vice -Chairperson? Where is he? Is he in the Chamber? We will go to Order No. 8 as the Chair comes to---

entries.label: heading
entries.text: THE NATIONAL DROUGHT MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) BILL (NATIONAL ASSEMBLY BILLS NO. 26 OF 2019)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I now order for the Division Bell to be rung for two minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: We need two Tellers because we are going to vote by Roll Call. Sen. Kang'ata and Sen. Mutula Kilonzo Jnr, will be the tellers. Sen. Sakaja, what is your intervention?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Johnson Arthur Sakaja
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I understand why you have sought for voting by Roll Call. However, I would like to indulge you, because for those of us who are here, we have our cards and looking at the number of Divisions we have, especially in the Committee of the Whole, that the names of the Members who are on the other side be noted, so that they can vote by Roll Call or they can tick their votes, but for the convenience of the House, those who are here be able to vote electronically. Mr. Speaker, Sir, you have the mandate and you can make that decision, so that we can move on to the real business that Members want to discuss.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I think that is a good suggestion; those who are in the Chamber can vote by pressing and those who are in the "Extended Chamber" will note.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: The Secretariat says, logistically, they are not ready for electronic voting because I have to feed in the question. So, we just have to do Roll Call voting. What is it, Sen. Sakaja?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Johnson Arthur Sakaja
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the Secretariat should be a bit creative. Many at times, even when we vote electronically, there are some Members who do not have cards. In those instances, those Members without cards are called "assisted voters." Mr. Speaker, Sir, for purposes of convenience, I wish the Secretariat was listening, because they are the ones proposing, just like the situations - I am glad the Clerks at the table are listening - where some Members do not have cards, but the rest vote electronically, we can make the assumption that those Members on the other side do not have a card so that the ones in the Chamber vote as the "assisted voters."

entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Hon. Senators, let us settle down. We are about to begin the Roll Call voting again. Please take your seats; it is going to be very fast. We will move fast by voting on the Orders one by one. I ask those in the extended Chamber to move forward because we are going to move very fast.

entries.label: speech
entries.text: Concerning The Pandemic Response and Management Bill (Senate Bills No.6 of 2020), we have four Divisions to take. Hon. Senators, I would like you to listen because we are going to vote on the four at the same time. When you come in, you will vote on all of them. If you have any reservations on one, you should mention. I would like to read the four. On Clauses for deletion, we have Clauses 3, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 29 and 40. Please note that the following amendments were dropped or rather withdrawn. We have Clause 20 by Sen. Mugo and Sen. Farhiya who had proposed a change and Clause 29 by Sen. Kang'ata and Sen. Mugo.

entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I beg to move that the House do agree with the Committee in the said report, and ask Sen. (Dr.) Zani to second.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Hon. Senators, since some clauses were rejected, the Bill will go to Mediation. Next Bill.

entries.label: heading
entries.text: THE NATIONAL DROUGHT MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) BILL (NATIONAL ASSEMBLY BILLS NO. 26 OF 2019)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Margaret Kamar
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I beg to report that the committee of the Whole has considered The National Drought Management Authority (Amendment) Bill (National Assembly Bills No. 26 of 2019) and its approval thereof without amendments.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Samuel Poghisio
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I beg to move that the House do agree with the Committee in the said report, and ask Sen. Dullo to second.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Samuel Poghisio
entries.text: Mr. Speaker Sir, I beg to move that The National Drought Management Authority (Amendment) Bill (National Assembly Bills No.26 of 2019) be now read a Third Time. I ask Sen. Dullo to second.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I now put the question; that The National Drought Management Authority (Amendment) Bill be now read a Third Time. The Division will be at the end. Hon. Senators, I direct that the Division Bell be rung for two minutes. We will be voting on the four Bills.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Senators! Take your seats. I will put the four questions. When you come to vote, you will vote on the four Bills, so that we save on time. I put the questions which are- That the Pandemic Response and Management Bill, (Senate Bills No.6 of 2020), The Kenya Medical Supplies Authority (Amendment) Bill (Senate Bills No.38 of 2018), the National Drought Management Authority (Amendment) Bill (National Assembly Bills No.26 of 2019; and, The Cancer Prevention and Control (Amendment) Bill (Senate Bills No.9 of 2019) be now read a Third Time. Voting is by Roll Call. You may proceed to vote.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Senators proceeded to vote by Roll Call)

entries.label: heading
entries.text: INVITATION TO SPEAKER'S KAMUKUNJI TO DISCUSS THE THIRD BASIS FOR REVENUE ALLOCATION

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, hon. Senators! One of the businesses that I gazetted to transact today is the Third Basis for Revenue Allocation Among the County Governments. However, the Report in the form it is cannot be tabled in this House today. I am, therefore, directing that we have a Kamukunji on Monday, so that we are taken through the Report, to build consensus before it is tabled.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text:
No. The report has not been tabled. After the

Kamukunji,

I will give further direction on when we will meet for the Report to be tabled and discussed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text:
Having said that and concluded business of the day, it is now time to adjourn the House. The Senate, therefore, stands adjourned until Tuesday, 7th July, 2020, at 2.30 p.m. For the Kamukunji on Monday, we shall meet at 11.00 a.m.

The Senate rose at 5.55 p.m.
